original_question: Must the torus decomposition of every algebraic sail in the sense of Klein contain at least one face that is integer congruent to a triangle, at least one face at integer distance 1 from the cone vertex, and at least one face at integer distance greater than 1 from the cone vertex?
correct_elements: Your draft identifies the exact target correctly: it matches Conjecture 12 in Section 3.3 almost verbatim. It has the right object of study (the torus decomposition of an algebraic sail in the sense of Klein) and the right three asserted features: existence of a face integer congruent to a triangle, existence of a face at integer distance 1 from the cone vertex, and existence of a face at integer distance greater than 1.
missing_details: The ambient setting is the real space R^n with the standard lattice Z^n; this is assumed globally in Sections 1 and 2.

An 'algebraic sail' is not any sail: in case [A] of Section 3.1 it means a sail of an algebraic cone, where the cone comes from the arrangement of invariant hyperplanes of a matrix A in SL_n(Z) whose characteristic polynomial is irreducible over Q and has only real roots.
The phrase 'in the sense of Klein' refers specifically to Klein sails/Klein polyhedra, defined in Definition 2.4 as the relevant sail construction for that choice of data.

The paper's notion of 'torus decomposition' is specialized: in the remark immediately before Conjecture 10 it is the collection of integer-congruence types of polyhedra in any fundamental domain of a periodic Klein sail, together with the integer distances of those faces to the cone vertex.
The term 'integer congruent' depends on Definition 1.1: two sets are integer congruent if one is sent to the other by an affine integer lattice transformation.
The term 'integer distance' also depends on Definition 1.1 and is not merely Euclidean distance.
The three existential requirements are separate; the paper does not say they must be realized by the same face.

To be fully stand-alone, the question should make explicit that algebraic sails are periodic via the Dirichlet subgroup action and that the factor-sail is homeomorphic to an (n-1)-torus in the totally real case.
refined_question: Let C be an algebraic cone in R^n in the sense of Section 3.1[A], namely a cone of the arrangement of invariant hyperplanes of some matrix A in SL_n(Z) whose characteristic polynomial is irreducible over Q and has only real roots, and let S be the corresponding Klein sail (Definition 2.4). Via the action of the Dirichlet subgroup of A, the factor-sail is an (n-1)-torus; its torus decomposition is the collection of integer-congruence classes of the polyhedral faces in a fundamental domain, each endowed with its integer distance from the cone vertex. Is it true that every such torus decomposition contains at least one face that is integer congruent (under an affine lattice automorphism) to a triangle, at least one face at integer distance 1 from the cone vertex, and at least one face at integer distance greater than 1 from the cone vertex?
justification: The draft is aiming exactly at Conjecture 12, not at a neighboring problem. The wording of Conjecture 12 in Section 3.3 is essentially the same as your draft. To make it stand-alone and faithful to the paper, one must import the definitions of integer congruence and integer distance from Definition 1.1, the Klein-sail setup from Definition 2.4, the meaning of 'algebraic' from case [A] in Section 3.1, and the meaning of 'torus decomposition' from the remark immediately before Conjecture 10. I therefore kept the statement at exactly the paper's scope and only unpacked those hidden assumptions and definitions.
